newsitem.title: USA: UST Inc says sees Q1 1997 below Q1 1996.
newsitem.headline: UST Inc says sees Q1 1997 below Q1 1996.

text.p: UST Inc said Monday it expected a drop in first quarter earnings primarily because of a decline in moist smokeless tobacco unit volume.

The company said it does not expect to acheive its target of 10 percent earnings per share growth for 1997 because of competitive pressures in the marketplace. It said it is premature to assess the effect on unit volume results for the remainder of the year.
UST said the first quarter would include a charge of $6.6 million from employment contracts for two former officers.
UST said also contributing to the decline was a one-time unit volume adjustment due to a change in the company's delivery pattern to wholesalers.
These factors will more than offset the anticipated additional unit volume generated by the first shipping day of the roll out of Copenhagen Long Cut at the end of the first quarter, UST said.

"United States Tobacco Company's strategic plans for 1997 and beyond remain focused on expanding the market for moist smokeless tobacco while addressing the competitive situation in the marketplace," said UST chairman and chief executive officer Vincent Gierer Jr. "Several initiatives are being considered for implementation at the appropriate time," he added.
The first quarter earnings report is expected to be released on April 17, 1997.
